summary.text: Amanda Pusczek is a registered nurse and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 4th Congressional District. According to her campaign website, she was born in Missouri, grew up in Alabama, and has more than a decade of clinical nursing experience, including psychiatric nursing. She has not previously held elected office and describes herself as a nurse rather than a career politician, running on health care and cost-of-living issues.

paragraphs.text: According to her campaign website, born in 1990 in Ferguson, Missouri; at age six she and her mother moved to Alabama, with a few years spent in Wiesbaden, Germany. She told a Walker County Democratic meeting in January 2026 that she was born in Missouri in 1990. (Her Ballotpedia survey profile lists Alabama as her birthplace.)

Graduated from public school with an Advanced Diploma in 2008, then earned an Associate Degree in Nursing at John C. Calhoun Community College (listed by Ballotpedia as 2014) and a bachelor's degree from Western Governors University in 2022.

Works as a nurse, with over a decade of clinical experience and a stated interest in psychiatric nursing and mental health advocacy. Her campaign website says she traveled to New York City during the COVID-19 outbreak while completing her bachelor's degree in nursing; she told the Walker County meeting her work included hospitals, prisons and schools.

Married her husband in 2022; her campaign website says Alabama's health-care and reproductive-rights restrictions affected the couple's family plans, and the Mountain Eagle reports that this and the 2024 election contributed to her decision to run.

Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for the 4th District; the Mountain Eagle reported in January 2026 that her opponent in that primary was Shane Weaver. She has no prior campaigns or offices listed.
Is affiliated with the American Nurses Association, 50501, the Madison County Democratic Party, Alabama Young Democrats, and Indivisible 5th District North Alabama.
